pr_title: Define algorithm providers in terms of plugins
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind cleanup
/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Define algorithm providers in terms of plugins rather than the legacy predicates/priorities keys. This practically makes the scheduler plugins-first instead of predicates/priorities-first.

This PR also defines a new algorithm registry named LegacyRegistry that maintains the old set of registered predicates and priorities. It is the same as the existing one that used to be defined as a set of global variables in ```pkg/scheduler/algorithm_factory.go```. The second commit merges ```ConfigProducerRegistry``` into ```LegacyRegistry``` (instead of being a member of it), and so  we end up with only three registries:

1) A ```framework.Registry``` for in-tree framework plugins defined in ```pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/registry.go```.

2) ```plugins.LegacyRegistry``` defined in ```pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/legacy_registry.go```, and contains predicates and priorities keys and how they map to plugins.

3) ```algorithmprovider.Registry``` defined in ```pkg/scheduler/algorithmprovider/registry.go```. A registry of algorithm providers (e.g., DefaultAlgorithmProvider, ClusterAutoscalerProvider) to their plugin configurations.


**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #86162

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```

/cc @Huang-Wei
